title: A retry after an unconfirmed refund sends a new idempotency key, so the same refund can be paid twice
evidence: refundSelected() creates a fresh key on every click (app.js:114-117, 128). api.js:32 says the key lets the server ignore a repeated request 'for the same attempt', but a retry is never the same attempt. On failure the catch block (app.js:131-133) keeps state.selected unchanged and the finally block re-enables the button (app.js:83, 135-137), so the user can click Refund again at once. The only guard is the sentence 'Reload and check the order statuses', which nothing enforces.
failing_case: Select 3 paid orders and confirm. The server issues the refunds, but the response is lost (fetch rejects, or a proxy returns 502/504 after the upstream succeeded). The UI shows 'The refund was not confirmed' with the same 3 rows still ticked and the button enabled. The user clicks Refund again and confirms. A new UUID is sent, the server treats it as a new request, and the customers are refunded twice.
remediation: Keep one key per intended refund (same ids and amount) and reuse it for a retry until a definitive answer arrives. After an ambiguous failure, reload the order statuses and clear or lock the selection before another refund can be sent.

title: A successful refund with an empty or non-JSON body is reported as 'not confirmed'
evidence: refund() goes through the shared request(), which always parses JSON. If POST /refunds answers 200 or 204 with no body, res.json() throws and request() raises ApiError('...not valid JSON'). app.js:131-133 then shows 'The refund was not confirmed' for a refund that went through. No contract in the payload says the endpoint returns a body.
failing_case: The proxy answers 204 No Content to POST /api/v1/refunds after refunding. The user sees an error, the toast and reload never run, the rows stay selected, and the user is invited to try again.
remediation: Let request() take a flag for endpoints with no body, or read res.text() and parse only when it is non-empty. Judge refund success by the status code.

requirement.why: The refund response format is not specified anywhere in the payload; 204 is a common answer for a POST action.

title: Orders that are already refunded, pending or of unknown status can be selected and sent for refund; the confirm dialog says money will go back
evidence: renderRow (app.js:34-45) renders a checkbox for every order whatever its status. The refund button is gated only on selection count and busy flags (app.js:83). No eligibility rule exists in domain.js. README lines 6-10 list what the server must check (permission, CSRF, idempotency) but not order state.
failing_case: Set Status to 'refunded', tick the 10 rows, click 'Refund 10 orders'. The dialog reads 'Refund 10 orders totalling $X. This sends money back to the customers.' and the POST is sent for orders that were already refunded. Whether this pays twice depends on a server rule that neither the code nor the README asks for.
remediation: Add a pure canRefund(order) in domain.js (status === 'paid'). Disable the checkbox for other statuses, and compute the confirm amount from the same function. Keep the server check as the real enforcement.

requirement.why: Refunding an order whose status is already 'refunded' is nonsensical; no document states the eligibility rule

title: normaliseOrder accepts a missing, null, empty or array total as $0 instead of dropping the record, contradicting its own contract
evidence: The comment at domain.js:7 promises null 'when ... no numeric total'. Number(null), Number(''), Number([]) and Number(false) are all 0, and Number.isFinite(0) is true (domain.js:12). Negative totals also pass. Traced from JS coercion rules. Node was not available to run it, since the shell was denied.
failing_case: The server sends {"id":7,"total":null,"status":"paid"}. The row shows $0.00, counts in Orders and the average, and can be ticked and refunded. The 'could not be shown because the data is incomplete' note never appears.
remediation: Accept only typeof raw.total === 'number' or a non-empty numeric string, require a finite value, and decide explicitly about negatives. Add a domain test for null, '', [] and false.

title: Revenue re-applies the gold discount and 8.25% sales tax in the browser on top of the server's order total
evidence: orderRevenueCents (domain.js:25-30) treats order.total as a pre-discount, pre-tax subtotal. It then applies a hardcoded tier discount and tax rate. The server owns the order total, which is the same figure the refund dialog sums (app.js:122). The Average stat also divides by all orders, including refunded and pending ones that count as 0 (domain.js:35). No document states the intended definitions.
failing_case: A standard-tier paid order with total 100.00 (already the charged amount) shows revenue $108.25. A gold order with total 90.00 shows $97.42. The Revenue card then disagrees with the sum of the Total column and with what the refund dialog shows for the same orders. Tax-rate or tier changes on the server drift silently.
remediation: Use the server-supplied total (or have the server return revenue). If the client must derive it, document in domain.js what 'total' includes and define Average as revenue over paid orders. Add tests with figures.

requirement.why: 'total' is the only money field the server sends and the refund dialog treats it as the amount paid; nothing says it is pre-tax

title: A failed reload after a confirmed refund leaves the refunded orders selected and the Refund button live
evidence: app.js:128-130 refunds, then calls load(). load() clears state.selected only on success (app.js:98). On failure it goes to the catch at app.js:105-108, and the finally at app.js:110 re-renders the button. refundSelected's finally (app.js:135-136) then sets refunding=false. state.selected still holds the ids and state.orders still holds the old rows, so renderRefundButton (app.js:83) enables the button as 'Refund N orders'. The same stale selection also survives a failed search load.
failing_case: Select 3 paid orders and confirm. The refund succeeds and the toast says 'Refunded 3 orders.' The follow-up GET /orders returns 500 or the connection drops. The table still shows the 3 rows checked, the error banner reads 'Orders could not be loaded', and 'Refund 3 orders' is enabled. A second click and confirm sends the same ids again with a new Idempotency-Key (see the idempotency finding). The customers can be refunded twice if the server does not also reject refunded orders. The README says only that the server honours the key.
remediation: Clear state.selected and mark or remove the refunded rows as soon as the refund is confirmed, before the reload. Also clear the selection, or disable the button, whenever a load fails, so the button never acts on rows the server may have changed.

title: Pressing Next or Previous on the last or first step disables the focused button, so focus is lost and the new page is not announced
evidence: renderTable (app.js:62-73) sets disabled on the button that was just activated. A disabled element cannot keep keyboard focus, and the document falls back to body. #page (index.html:34) is not a live region, so the change of page is silent too. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order and 4.1.3 Status Messages.
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to Next and presses Enter on page 2 of 3. Page 3 renders, Next becomes disabled, and focus returns to the top of the document. The user has to tab through the whole toolbar to reach Previous. A screen reader says nothing about the page change.
remediation: Use aria-disabled and keep the button focusable, or move focus to the table caption or the page indicator after paging. Make #page a role=status region, or announce 'Page N of M' through the existing message region.

quote: setMessage(`Orders could not be loaded. ${err.message}`, true);
title: After a failed search the table, stats and Refund button keep showing the previous results as if they matched the current query
evidence: In the catch block of load() (app.js:105-108) state.orders, state.selected and the table are not touched. renderRefundButton() in finally keeps the button enabled if rows were selected (app.js:110, 83). The search box and status filter already hold the new values.
failing_case: Load the page (all orders). Choose Status 'pending' and the request returns 500. A red message appears, but the table still lists the 'All' rows, the stats are unchanged, and previously ticked rows stay ticked. The Refund button stays enabled for rows the filter says should not be on screen. The user can refund from a stale view.
remediation: On a load failure, clear state.orders, state.selected and the table (or mark them stale and disable selection and Refund), and show the error in place of the rows with a Retry control.

title: The page title is 24 px left of the content column on wide screens
evidence: main is max-width 1100 with box-sizing border-box and 24 px padding, so its content starts at (viewport-1100)/2 + 24. The h1 sits in the header's content box (header padding 24) and is itself 1100 wide, centred, so it starts at (viewport-1100)/2. Traced from the CSS, not rendered, since the shell was denied.
failing_case: At 1360 px the h1 left edge is at 130 px, while the stat cards, toolbar and table start at 154 px.
remediation: Set .top h1 to max-width: 1052px, or wrap both in the same container class with the same padding.
